files.name: m_spi_master.sv

open_points: Section 4 / REQ-PAR-001 (SPI-4-03): the elaboration error for an illegal PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV is a generate-if with $error. RTL_RULES RR-11 does not allow system tasks in checked code, so the check sits inside `ifndef SYNTHESIS`. Simulation and lint tools (Verilator) stop elaboration with an error message. Yosys defines SYNTHESIS, so it skips the check and a synthesis run with an illegal value does not fail by itself. I chose this because it is the only portable elaboration error that keeps to RR-11 (an undefined-module trick also fails Verilator lint for legal values). The reviewer should approve this ifndef block.

Section 13 / REQ-IMP-006 (SPI-13-08, SPI-13-09): o_sclk is written as a hazard-free mux, (cs_n & i_cpol) | (~cs_n & r_sclk) | (i_cpol & r_sclk). Synthesis may remove the redundant consensus term. Keeping it needs a dont_touch or hand-instantiated cell in the implementation flow, which is outside the RTL. Functionally, r_sclk is loaded with i_cpol at the burst-start edge and equals CPOL_b at the edge where o_cs_n rises. So the mux inputs are equal whenever o_cs_n changes, unless i_cpol was changed against ENV-003.

Section 7.1 / REQ-CMD-005, REQ-IMP-007: o_cmd_ready is decoded combinationally from flip-flops only: state, the half-period counter, the captured i_cmd_last and o_rsp_valid. It has no path from any input, as REQ-IMP-007 allows ('logic of flip-flops only'). It is not one dedicated flip-flop, so in silicon it can glitch briefly after a clock edge. I took the specification's allowance as the reading.

Section 7.7 / DEC-004 with CPHA_b = 1: bit r[0] is sampled at SCLK edge 16, the same edge where the response is loaded. So the response byte is formed from {rx_shift[6:0], i_miso} and written straight into o_rsp_data or the held register. i_miso therefore goes through a 2:1 mux into those data flip-flops, with no synchroniser, as REQ-IMP-008 asks. I read this as compatible with 'captured directly into a data flip-flop'.

Section 7 / REQ-CMD-007, REQ-RST-010: the half-period counter also counts the D-1 blocked Idle cycles after o_cs_n rises. On reset it is set to D-1, so o_cmd_ready = 1 at the first edge after reset release (no blocked cycles across reset, OQ-006).

Section 6.2 / REQ-IMP-003: all flip-flops, including data-only registers (shift registers, held byte, CPOL_b/CPHA_b), are reset asynchronously to 0. The specification gives reset values only for the outputs, so resetting everything is the conservative reading.

Section 7.6 / REQ-MISO-004: the receive shift register is not cleared between transfers. Each transfer shifts in exactly 8 new samples before its byte is formed, so the byte contains only that transfer's bits (REQ-MISO-005).
notes:
I wrote `m_spi_master` as one file. It has not been compiled, linted or simulated here; the RR-40 lint and RR-43 synthesis checks have not been run.

**What the module contains:**
- **Phase state machine.** A 4-state FSM (Idle, Transfer, Pause, Trail) is the core.
- **Counters.** An 8-bit half-period counter compares against D-1. In Idle the same counter counts the D-1 cycles where `o_cmd_ready` is held at 0 after `o_cs_n` rises. A 4-bit counter counts the SCLK edges in each transfer.
- **Data paths.** A transmit shift register drives `o_mosi`, and a receive shift register samples `i_miso`. The response stream has one shown byte and one held byte.
- **SPI mode.** `i_cpol`/`i_cpha` are captured at the edge where a burst starts.
- **Outputs.**
  - `o_cs_n` and `o_mosi` come straight from flip-flops.
  - `o_sclk` follows `i_cpol` while `o_cs_n` is 1 and comes from the internal SCLK flip-flop while `o_cs_n` is 0. The mux is written to avoid glitches.
  - `o_cmd_ready` is decoded from flip-flops only, with no path from any input.

**Points the reviewer should look at:**
- **Illegal `PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV`.** The elaboration error uses `$error`, so it sits inside `ifndef SYNTHESIS` to keep to rule RR-11. Simulation and lint stop on an illegal value, but a Yosys synthesis run does not fail by itself.
- **Requirement IDs.** Only IDs listed in REQUIREMENTS.md are used. Rules that bind the testbench or environment (SPI-11-*, SPI-12-*) and SPI-13-01/12 are not tagged in the RTL.
